section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1968
title: Incidence of suicidal deaths in States, Union Territories Cities. The regional distribution of suicidal deaths indicated marked variations from State to State. Table 9 presents the actual incidence of such deaths during 1967 and 1968 along with the percentage variations from 1967 to 1968. A rise of 67·1% and 82·2% was noticed in Kerala and Bihar respectively. Among the Union Territories, Pondicherry indicated a rise of 54·7% against an over-all decrease of 23·0% in all the Union Territories taken together. Big cities like Bombay, Calcutta and Delhi reported decreases, while Ahmedabad reported a sharp rise of 81·6%. notes: The maximum incidence of suicides was noticed in the State of West Bengal (5,744) followed by Tamil Nadu (5,617) and U.P. (4,471) accounting for 14.1%, 13.8% and 10.9% of the total suicides reported in the country respectively. Only 43 cases of suicides were registered in Jammu and Kash.
